verdict.tagline: Rough physics and technical crashes challenge early attempts at combat.
for_you_if: you enjoy mastering complex physics-based combat controls
you are willing to practice challenging mouse-driven mechanics
not_for_you_if: you need stable frame rates on release hardware
you cannot tolerate progression wipes and physics bugs
you require clear guidance and a structured story

distortion_flags.sentence: Initial frustration with controls and crashes gives way to higher satisfaction as players adapt to the physics system over extended playtimes.

cohorts.label: <2h refund window
cohorts.summary: Players struggle with terrain collisions, awkward recoveries after knockdowns, and confusing navigation without clear guidance.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that characters get stuck, slip, or break bones easily upon colliding with terrain or objects in the environment.

citations.review_text:
This has gotta be the worst game I've been in the last few months. It's just unplayable in a literal sense for 2 reasons.

1. Damage is insane for minor things. If you walk in to a wall, even with damage to player turned to zero, your skull gets caved in. Bump your arm in to a wall? Shattered to a million pieces. You can't progress unless you have a helmet which is insane.

2. Fatal Errors every 5 minutes. I've done every tutorial on the face of the planet, including the one on the official Discord, and I still get Fatal Errors if I stub my toe too hard.

I'll play it again in a while when its actually playable for longer than 5 minutes and all the bugs are patched. DO NOT GET THIS IN ITS CURRENT STATE!

Returned this disappointed. The improved graphics and mechanics are nice, but that's about it. The progression is not only slow but very unclear, the horrible UI does not help with that either. 

The different materials are not explained at all, and after playing for a bit I could not figure out why they even mattered in the first place. I honestly didn't notice a weight change between anything, even when making weapons larger. The entire crafting bit is a fun idea, but the UI is just downright awful, like seriously, its one thing to not explain your crafting system, its another to almost make it downright unpleasant to use.

As for the maps, the basement was the only one that was consistent and that I enjoyed. Every other map/scenario was either boring, or extremely glitchy. In the middle of fighting my characters feet would often slip or shake when interacting with some parts of the terrain, this would either lead to me losing or my character just getting stuck. The same thing would also happen to the NPCs.

Overall not worth the 25 dollars at all for what you're getting here. It feels like the game went through a large change in development, switching from a fighting sim to a rage slop game. Trust me when I say this but the Tech Demo is far more enjoyable, it's easier to jump in, scratch that itch, rather than worrying about a very unclear un-fun progression system that hardly even rewards you for the repetitive gameplay. Not to mention the repeated crashing has barely been fixed. Would love to see this game improve, as the mechanics and gameplay are so uniquely enjoyable, but there needs to be a lot of changes before that.

Getting back up takes like ten years but the AI do it way faster, and tripping causes you to break your foot. Plus the game loves throwing uneven terrain at you.
I decided to refund the game after tripping over a barrel because I walked by it on an errand. My character bumped it lightly as he got up. This caused him to break his foot, keeping him stuck to the ground until I gave up the errand.
Picking up objects from the ground also seems even more difficult than the demo... If you knock an AI to the ground, you'd be lucky to win. But if you get knocked down, it's game over.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that once a character is knocked down, it is nearly impossible to recover control or get back up while enemies attack.

citations.review_text:
Combat feels clunky and somehow less responsive than the early demos. Progression mode is pretty unfun to get started in, too. Most people you run into will have weapons like hoes that can one shot you when the game only gives you one handed knives, axes, or awful wooden shovels that are still half the length of the enemy's weapon. 

Getting knocked down in a fight is unfun. There's no ability to ground fight, or defend yourself for long enough to get back up. Your character ragdolls and you nearly lose all control. In the early demo you could at least try to get back up but in current gameplay you just feel like a sack of bricks on the floor if you ever get knocked down, and you have to watch as the enemy wails on you and kills you. 

Weapon physics in general have gotten worse. Half the time it feels like enemies do 5x the damage with their weapons, and when you use certain one handed or blunt weapons against them, you feel like you are wacking them with a stale bread stick. Yet, they use the same weapon on you, and they can instantly knock you down with a hit to the shoulder, or one shot kill you with a random sickle. Don't get me started on how certain weapons can also seemingly clip straight through plate/chainmail, and when they do, they will also one shot you. 

They've improved performance a lot. The game looks and runs well, and I can fight more than 2 enemies without the game crapping itself now, but what good is that when the core combat is so dreadful? The progression isn't even fun. It feels like they're just copying Exanima when it comes to the core gameplay loop, but they're doing it worse. Half of the fights you lose don't feel fair, and half of the fights you win feel too fast or luck-based as well. I know some people will call it a "skill issue" but genuinely, the combat is just not polished enough yet.

Getting back up takes like ten years but the AI do it way faster, and tripping causes you to break your foot. Plus the game loves throwing uneven terrain at you.
I decided to refund the game after tripping over a barrel because I walked by it on an errand. My character bumped it lightly as he got up. This caused him to break his foot, keeping him stuck to the ground until I gave up the errand.
Picking up objects from the ground also seems even more difficult than the demo... If you knock an AI to the ground, you'd be lucky to win. But if you get knocked down, it's game over.

cohorts.label: 2-20h
cohorts.summary: Reviewers encounter severe physics clipping issues, crashes, and steep learning curves with unexplained mechanics.

claims.claim: Reviewers experience physics bugs where characters, weapons, and items clip through the floor or terrain, sometimes instantly killing the player.

citations.review_text:
I understand that this game is in early access and I will admit, the early access does perform better then the demo. Although, there are still TONS of problems with the physics of this game. I have lost count of how many times I have had my weapon(s) clip through the floor and get stuck, I also occasionally clip into the NPCs when they grapple (if I am lucky enough to escape I usually end up with 2 dislocated/broken limbs forcing me to forfeit the fight), or every now and again I will get hit by a large stronger NPC and it will look like I am in the middle of an earthquake eventually causing me to clip into the ground.

Once again I do understand that this is in early access but so far it doesn't seem like much has been done to fix these specific issues. I'm sure the developers are working hard to fix the bugs in their game but . . . in it's current state, I don't think I would recommend anyone buy the game until it is more polished.

While i think the game is fun to play at times, there's just to many glitches and unfair gameplay mechanics that make it unenjoyable at times. I died while in the knight tourney and glitched into the coffin killing me without even giving me a chance to get up. It's WAY too easy to break your bones, I try to kneel down to grab armor off a guy, and BOOM, my legs broken. Also, whenever I drop a weapon on the path in the forest map it just disappears into the ground, and I cant find it anywhere. 6/10, i definitely see a bright future for the game. and glitches are to be expected, considering the game is not that old, but the glitches make me think quitting is the better option than wasting an hour trying to progress only to die to a glitch.

It's insane the devs think this game is worth over $20, becuase for months half sword has been a buggy mess, arguably worse than the demo, yet they still charge an amount I'd expect for a 1.0 release. 

Also, even after a recent series of important updates that convinced me to buy half sword, I am still met with run ending bugs (pulling stuff out of my belt flings me across the map, my arm will twist and break sometimes when spawning in with/picking up a longarm, and just terrible physics in general) that makes this otherwise interesting, engaging game into a miserable joke with a $30 price tag.

Even if there are significant improvements from the demo they do not justify this game's cost, hopefully this will change soon, if the recent burst of updates are anything to go by.

Overall, ignoring bugs, a 7/10. Regardless, save your money and wait for the devs to make it worth it.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game suffers from crashes, long loading times, and performance issues that require lowering graphic settings.

citations.review_text: Strongly not recommend, it's terribly broken, crashing, maps loading so long you die before you see anything, ragdoll controls like in games from 2007

This is the worst performing game i have played in a decade. Unplayable for the most part. Settings also don't change, or stay changed. Massive hitches and screen tearing. 
The best part is, the demo ran pretty much fine for me. 
If the game didn't teleport enemies into me, due to terrible performance, it would be pretty damn fun.

The late game is so damn broken I almost threw my keyboard across the room multiple times.  Its SO much fun, right up until you get to fully armored opponents and then it makes absolutely no sense.  Every movement you make feels like you're surrounded by quicksand, which would be understandable in a full suit of armor, except none of your opponents have the same problem.  God forbid if you have a two handed weapon because you will 1000% never be able to use it.  It will get caught on every single thing around you, especially your own body where you hold it behind your back, and you'll consistently drop it. When you DO land a strike, you might as well be swinging a wet towel around because it does zero damage to anyone.  Meanwhile, if you even brush up against an enemy's weapon, whether they're actually swinging it or not, and regardless if you're wearing a full suit of armor, you'll instantly lose a limb or have your neck cut wide open because apparently they're actually lightsabers.

Lastly, I have a pretty damn strong PC and GPU but have to run the game on Low or else it's essentially 5 FPS.  Also, it'll crash over and over when you try to remove enemies armor after you defeat them.

You should buy this for the first few tiers of play because it IS very fun, but anything beyond mid-game content is extremely broken and frustrating

claims.claim: Reviewers state that core progression systems, crafting mechanics, and user interface elements are unexplained or unintuitive.

citations.review_text: The gameplay is so good but the UI is horrible. nothing is explained, no clear progression on armor.

Came back for the new update but it's still more irritating than fun. Still less enjoyable than the "tech demo" overall.

Enemies rush into you weirdly fast and grab you, and when your bodies collide, theirs is usually a brick wall, and you just crumple into the ground.

The zombies in the abyss latch onto you like a magnet and bite you until death through your armor.

Also, and maybe this one is mostly me but, too many of the games features are unexplained and unintuitive. The crafting UI is a bizarre mess, not to mention it's unclear what the use is of the various material types. Does anyone actually use this? Maybe only in the late progression? I unlocked the ability to craft swords, saved up over 200 pfennings (money) and crafted the biggest sword I could which was still shorter than a sword that costs far less from the trader and felt like it had no weight behind it at all. 

I remember people saying that the reason you feel weak and uncoordinated in this game as opposed to the demo is because there's some sort of system by which you gain strength as you character progresses. Exactly how does this work? Why can't I see that progress, and why do I still feel like a baby foal 3 ranks in? What's the point of this system existing and being a secret?

Most weapons feel like you're limply flopping them at the enemy, but the enemies feel extremely solid. You do NOT want to get near them, yet they're constantly rushing you.

Weaponry feels really imbalanced. I got the flail one time and I felt nearly invincible, but the longstaff feels like it's made out of plastic. In its current state, it feels like you're at a major disadvantage in every possible fight and you're trying to find the right strategy to cautiously cheese out wins.

Most of the fights in the progression mode are seriously undesirable to do. It gives you list of several possible encounters to choose from to make money and progress further in the rank, but who wants to do an encounter where you have to win…

citations.review_text: this game is a lot like ark to me. its the first to do what its doing but I feel like they lost steam and ran out of time. the game crashes every 15mins, some times your weapon will feel like a butter knife while if the enemy hits you its like a light saber. Great game. Before the recent updates, the game was very unoptimized (the forest, slums, and alley maps), but now its the third most played game I own on Steam.

I adored the original demo and was really excited to see what the full release would reveal. The new games are fun, the ui is beautifully created and makes me feel like I'm in medieval times, the ability to dislocate joints in combat is a welcome and very fun mechanic and the customisation of weapons and armour is so abundant I am overwhelmed with the quantity of choices, but nonetheless giddy. Despite this, there are major flaws that I cannot pass. The fps issues are abundant, mentioned heavily by other reviews and immediately seen once entering the game, characters are severely unoptimised, the new faces appear to not wrap properly around injuries when you break the skin and maps are so unoptimised that they cause my PC to get hot to a point where in summer I'm almost burnt by touching the metal at the back, despite having no problem with Elden Ring. There's also seemingly data leaks as while paused and tabbed out my computer whirrs and overheats to the point that I have to sometimes turn off the game if I cannot go immediately back to a round in fear of damaging my computer. The concept of a rework of the graphics in theory sounds reasonable, but every texture has been overdeveloped to a point where even on the lowest possible settings, massive performance issues are caused, bottlenecking a large portion of their community on lower end computers. The gore system is identical to the demo minus a few ways that bodies interact with bleeding and the actual separation during parts being cut off, but for some reason damaged skin layers no longer have a rough, meaty texture. This makes it so a shallow wound that in the demo would've been very visible, due to essentially being a small removed section of skin, is instead just a dark red texture that is layered over which in my opinion, just makes getting small injuries significantly less cool looking. Originally, in the demo eyes were separated to the layers of blood or damage, meaning that if you were soaked in blood you…

Smelly peasant with big pokey stick bash stooopid knight! 

Saw this game on social media and it looked fun....and it it! Its a steep learning curve at first for those not used to the realistic physics and mouse controls, but there's lots of great mindless "take your brains out" violence! Its initial controls I think might throw a lot of people and cause frustration, but once you start getting it right, it's so great. Cannot stress how satisfying it is to get that perfect "one swing kill" first swing out of the stalls. Also the ability to steal other weapons and armour off defeated combatants is a great touch! "damn that's a nice axe....YOINK!"

Yes there are issues with the game. It's a small dev team who defo need to communicate a little more. Some of the maps are badly optimised and may run like a dog on some lower cards (My RTX 4090 occasionally has issues, even on medium and low settings), but they are working on that. Can be frustrating when your weapons glitch in the wall or floor, but rarely happens, and that the downside of these types of real physics games. 

Gameplay is better with recent update. Honestly, bought it for ~£20 as I thought i'd support the devs. I've played 38 hours or so and still having a blast. If you're cautious, try the demo and hang on for a sale, but for such a small team, its defo scratched a itch a lot of people had. If it's in your budget, give it a go, and give it some time, especially to learn the art of the controls. Patience and timing are key.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe physics interactions that can feel janky or cause limbs and weapons to malfunction.

citations.review_text: This game is super fun and very engaging with its physics. A little janky, but fun!

the reviews have become more positive again, but as a long time fan of the game I feel it still has a long way to go. I'll say the game is still fun in its current state as a low-stakes turn-off-your-brain physics game - I personally enjoy this type of gameplay - but don't expect anything more than that.

some issues I have come across:
- The game crashes quite often still, though the recent performance patches have made it a lot more playable.
- the menus are still bad, strangely, they have sorting for one menu but not the rest.
- the game gets really dark sometimes but theres literally no brightness option.
- among many other quality of life features/options which are lacking in general.
- item pick up is pick up, inventory, and foundational features remain basic and unchanged from the original game.
- the combat has gotten better but some things are still left to be desired for the physics, which often glitches out.

Overall, why it is an improvement over the demo, it is only marginal and only after months of wait. I want to trust the developers but I just cannot be so quick to do so after the 4ish months of radio silence, the developers competence is also questionable to me, regardless of how big their team is, or whether it is in early access or not.

The game runs on UE5, so it's expected to be clunky and buggy in the Early Access stages... But so far, the developers have shown great effort with patching the game and optimization every update. 

The gameplay is very fun if you're into accurate medieval combat, with a hint of exaggerated flair. I think that the physics based combat is really fun, and the game is very fun overall. 

With how the physics work overall it's generally very satisfying to get certain hits in with some weapons, like using a sword to stab an enemy who is armored head-to-toe in the armpit, or using a dagger to slide in-between the gap in someone's face plate, but the most satisfying is landing parries with a longsword in my opinion... But the physics also makes it feel VERY hard to do things consistently, requiring LOTS of practice in order to feel like you're making any progress with fighting armored opponents consistently, without having to rely on just swinging your mouse randomly and confusing the game's AI. (Which is a good thing!)

However, because of the nature of the physics it can also be quite janky in some areas, like for example on the forest map there's a wagon pulling a cart that occasionally has some chests that contain valuables inside that you can either sell or equip to your character... But with how the physics work, you cannot jump into the cart, you instead have to drag a dead horse corpse all the way over to the cart, shimmy your way onto it, and then *somehow* knock yourself into the cart. I have only done this ONE time and it is VERY inconsistent and does not feel like it's worth the effort. The jumping system feels very confusing overall to me, but maybe I just need to experiment more... 

ANYWAYS, overall this is a VERY good game and I'd say if you're a person who likes high-stakes gameplay and a high learning curve, then this is the game for you! I'd rate this a solid 8/10 (As of current Early Access)

The gameplay is very fun if you're into accurate medieval combat, with a hint of exaggerated flair. I think that the physics based combat is really fun, and the game is very fun overall. 

With how the physics work overall it's generally very satisfying to get certain hits in with some weapons, like using a sword to stab an enemy who is armored head-to-toe in the armpit, or using a dagger to slide in-between the gap in someone's face plate, but the most satisfying is landing parries with a longsword in my opinion... But the physics also makes it feel VERY hard to do things consistently, requiring LOTS of practice in order to feel like you're making any progress with fighting armored opponents consistently, without having to rely on just swinging your mouse randomly and confusing the game's AI. (Which is a good thing!)

However, because of the nature of the physics it can also be quite janky in some areas, like for example on the forest map there's a wagon pulling a cart that occasionally has some chests that contain valuables inside that you can either sell or equip to your character... But with how the physics work, you cannot jump into the cart, you instead have to drag a dead horse corpse all the way over to the cart, shimmy your way onto it, and then *somehow* knock yourself into the cart. I have only done this ONE time and it is VERY inconsistent and does not feel like it's worth the effort. The jumping system feels very confusing overall to me, but maybe I just need to experiment more... 

ANYWAYS, overall this is a VERY good game and I'd say if you're a person who likes high-stakes gameplay and a high learning curve, then this is the game for you! I'd rate this a solid 8/10 (As of current Early Access)

claims.claim: Reviewers state that mastering the physics-based combat and mouse controls requires significant time, patience, and practice.

citations.review_text: This is an excellent game, it takes a bit to become good, but the game gets progressively more fun as your skill increases. Highly recommended! Seriously, buy the game.

This game is the pinnacle of medieval fighting simulators. It's ridiculous charming, and difficult to master. Sure, you could swing your sword haphazardly, but to wield your blade with skill, grace, and beauty takes insane amounts of time to become in any way consistent with it. While hard, the satisfaction of parrying only to reposte into their neck is unmatched. The game is early access, and sometimes that shows, but it's solid for how early it is, and I cannot recommend this game enough. If you like HEMA, this game is for you.

Once you get used to the mouse controls, this game is pure carnage fun. Swords feel lethal, blunts feel brutal. The early game is tough. But they give you an area to spar non-lethal opponents to train and bulk up, since you start as a shrimp.

Smelly peasant with big pokey stick bash stooopid knight! 

Saw this game on social media and it looked fun....and it it! Its a steep learning curve at first for those not used to the realistic physics and mouse controls, but there's lots of great mindless "take your brains out" violence! Its initial controls I think might throw a lot of people and cause frustration, but once you start getting it right, it's so great. Cannot stress how satisfying it is to get that perfect "one swing kill" first swing out of the stalls. Also the ability to steal other weapons and armour off defeated combatants is a great touch! "damn that's a nice axe....YOINK!"

Yes there are issues with the game. It's a small dev team who defo need to communicate a little more. Some of the maps are badly optimised and may run like a dog on some lower cards (My RTX 4090 occasionally has issues, even on medium and low settings), but they are working on that. Can be frustrating when your weapons glitch in the wall or floor, but rarely happens, and that the downside of these types of real physics games. 

Gameplay is better with recent update. Honestly, bought it for ~£20 as I thought i'd support the devs. I've played 38 hours or so and still having a blast. If you're cautious, try the demo and hang on for a sale, but for such a small team, its defo scratched a itch a lot of people had. If it's in your budget, give it a go, and give it some time, especially to learn the art of the controls. Patience and timing are key.

A brutal, difficult and (still) janky arena medieval combat simulator.
If you give it enough time and patience, the combat system becomes quite intuitive and extremely satisfying.
In the current early-access state there is no storyline, a little bit of progression system with combat tiers, but the biggest selling point to me is definitely the physics engine and what you can do with it - it's highly freeform and intentional.
Based on your weapon/hand movement and placement you can parry incoming blows, riposte and lop off limbs and heads. Hand movement is finnicky and sensitive, but when it clicks you can have satisfying cinematic swordfights or brutal melees, whatever floats your boat.
Performance wise, even with my PC, the game can choke when there are more NPCs on the field, you might get crashes, even progression save might get wiped - it happened to me once.
It's unfinished, but cheap and worth the price if you think about 60-80 dollar games that are also buggy and sell cut content for additional 20 dollars.
Definitely get it if you're patient and like medieval games.

claims.claim: Reviewers mention that progression save data can be unexpectedly wiped or reset.

citations.review_text: really great game and mechanics but every time i reload the game my progress resets really annoying

Hey, we have a physics based medieval sword-fighting game that sword nerds like for some reason, what can we do to improve it? Oh, how about we add an unavoidable zombie mode that you have to beat repeatedly to not permanently lose your save? To be clear, I've been playing a single save almost my entire playtime, however, it's extremely annoying to die to a physics bug (literally exploding) and be met with "46 souls seek revenge" and then you have to just sit there and kill 46 zombies that sometimes take an upwards of a minute in between to spawn and by the time you finally finish killing all 46 zombies you don't even feel like playing the game anymore. That's what happened to me anyways. Game was better in its demo (I had many hours in the demo) and somehow the combat gets worse with every update. With some mechanics they have added it really just seems like the devs just hate the idea of fun. On top of all of that the game runs like hot garbage and I had to use frame gen for decent framerate even on a relatively high end pc. Unfortunately I genuinely can't recommend anyone purchase this in the state it is. 

Edit: Tried to play the game a single time after writing this review and my completed progression save data was randomly wiped and it wanted me to make a new character. Don't feel like completing the high tier fights again because they feel like slamming your head in a car door repeatedly so I think that's the last time I boot. I loved this game in its demo and have given it so many chances.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features bugs and errors in abyss mode that can force character recreation or cause progress loss.

citations.review_text: I've had enough of this poor game. When playing the abyss mode, I'm constantly interrupted by game errors, forcing me to recreate my character. Also, when will you fix the bone fracture bug? Sometimes, my arm gets broken by air in the game.

I genuinely love this game and have been following it for a looong time. It's good but the bugs are so bad that I don't even play some of the game modes anymore cuz I don't wanna lose progress. It's so bad and downright unplayable at times that I've had to go to hospitals cuz of what I do to myself in moments of frustration. 3/10 if I'm being generous - it's got potential, but it sure as hell isn't a good game yet.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that running the game requires a capable modern PC due to optimization demands.

citations.review_text: Rough launch, great recovery. Horrible optimization at first but has come back around, even then you still need a decent PC to run it. I was an avid enjoyer of the demo & playtest, so I'm glad that it didn't stay that way forever, and actually became a full-fledged game

Most poorly optimized and buggiest game available right now, literally nothing compares to this mess, do not play unless you have a modern CPU and GPU, the only system requirements that are actually accurate is the amount of RAM required to play, because graphics card or CPU is capable of handling this game.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the combat system as physics-driven, where weapon control is managed by holding the left mouse button and moving the mouse.

citations.review_text:
This is, for me, the only combat game I would recommend, aside from other few.
Basically my amusement comes from it being a physics driven movement rather than animation combat.

There is no sequense and is not a combat game where you win by being the fastest input, each encounter is different between each other and dynamic.

it also has a progression mode which acts very much as roguelike/roguelite mecchanics, even having the possibility to transfer your gear into the Free mode where thesettings of combat are configurable.

There is fre other physics-combat-driven games oh there, and this one is the best of its kind. The World setting being XV is interesting too, many different lodouts combination. Multiplayer is achvabale/in the works. Work is being made and I love that everything has been worked with great care. 

My only recommendation would be to give values to sliders, and, to give name to frips,pommels, guards and blade profiles, in my opinnion that would incentivize community shared lodouts, which are posible based on images alone right now too.

Been following work since Demo, take care and thanks.

It's one of the best games ever, imo.

There isn't a great deal of content, in all honesty. If it was another game, I doubt I would have played more than 10-15 hours of it, but ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ this game is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ addictive. I played the original demo, the playtest, and now EA. I probably have around 200+ hours on the game in total, and istg most of it is just me doing the same thing over and over again, and for one simple reason: fighting is so much [u] fun. [/u]

The game is completely physics-based, and you control the character's weapon by holding LMB and moving your mouse. It is not an easy game to get the hang-of by any measure, but it's also not really that hard [i] once [/i] you get used to it. When you understand the foundations of the combat system, and you get some familiarity with the additional mechanics, weapons, etc., the game is more just about practice, and even then, usually a great deal of luck lmao.

Half-Sword is completely unhinged, tbh. 

It allows you to be an honourable knight, showing mercy, and sparing death, to those you defeat in battle, but on the other hand, it also allows you to unleash the most sadistic parts of yourself. You [u] will [/u] feel shame when you look in the mirror, but that's probably a good sign for you as a person, on the whole. 

The game features anatomically correct bodies (mostly - no peens to slice ;-; ), including organs, muscles, and skeleton. Not only that, but Half-Sword is so dedicated to creating their ultra-realistic HEMA-based fighting game that they made sure to code anatomically correct cutting, bruising, snapping, and breaking. Wherever you cut with a sword will be wherever you draw blood, or sever parts, from. If you hit an artery, blood literally spurts everywhere, coating you, your victim, and the floor. Wherever you hit with a mace will bruise and fracture. Enough damage can cause joints to snap, and even bones to break. On top of these real-life components, there is screaming, and lots of it.
